text:
maya: ran perf + flamegraph on host-rtg-12 (dedicated cluster). seeing a recurring hotspot in the tokenization path during 2k tok seqs. attaching quick logs.
kevin: can you paste the collapsed flame or perf script you used? quick glance: is this the pyalloc spike we saw last week?
maya: here's the command i ran: `perf record -F 99 -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > fg.svg` — the flame shows a big red block at `tokenize->unicode_decode->PyUnicode_New` (surprising for model-infer host)
juan: hmm, that points to Python heap churn. which tokenizer variant? huggingface fast? python tokenizers vs rust binding?
maya: using our runtime-binding that wraps HF tokenizers but falls back to python slow path for some custom normalizers. looks like some inputs trigger the slow path.
sophie: could also be GIL contention with the scheduler threads. did you capture thread-level callstacks? `perf` was system-wide but we need per-thread stacks and annotate idle/wait states.
maya: captured thread ids in the perf data. flame shows `sched_yield` interspersed; when I overlay `perf top -p <pid>` during a run it spikes in `Py_Malloc` as well.
perf-bot: perf-run summary: host-rtg-12 | 2025-10-02T14:03Z | samples: 120k | top frames: PyUnicode_New (18%), tokenize_loop (12%), scheduler_spin (9%), memcpy (7%).
kevin: scheduler_spin? that's our batching scheduler in C++ right? maybe spin-waiting while waiting for kvcache frames to be ready.
juan: could be caused by kernel selection fallback: if GPU kernel is busy we decode more on CPU (prefetch fallback) which increases tokenization throughput and causes queue pressure. any perfetto/nsys traces for the GPU side to correlate?
maya: i ran a short nsys timeline: it shows frequent kernel launches but several kernel retries with `cudaLaunchKernel` latency and some `cudaMemcpyAsync` spikes coinciding with CPU-side spikes. attaching a small excerpt.
lisa: if KV cache fetches are falling back to CPU copy due to page faults or evictions, that would increase CPU latency. Do we have kvcache miss counters for that timeframe?
maya: kvcache metrics: miss_rate ~ 0.012, evictions up by 4x vs baseline during the test (we had a small stress test with 32 concurrent streams). evictions line up with the PyUnicode/New spike windows.
kevin: hypothesis: frequent small evictions cause our prefetcher to trigger synchronous CPU copies for rehydration, which runs tokenizer+normalizer on the caller thread while holding locks -> causes GIL contention and Py alloc churn.
sophie: can we try two quick experiments: 1) disable the python slow-normalizer path (force rust fast tokenizer) and 2) increase kvcache capacity to avoid evictions for the same workload
maya: i ran experiment 1 on a replica: Py object churn drops, tokenize flame shrinks significantly, scheduler_spin decreases by ~60%. latency p50 down 8%.
juan: good. experiment 2? results?
maya: with kvcache cap +20% evictions drop to baseline and CPU hotspots disappear. however this increases GPU memory pressure and sometimes triggers kernel selection to switch to smaller-kernel (higher-latency) variant under memory pressure.
kevin: so tradeoff: larger kvcache reduces CPU overhead but forces different kernel selection on GPU which can increase tail latency. need smarter routing: prefer larger kvcache on hosts with spare GPU memory, otherwise prefer kernel variant that's less memory-hungry and accept some CPU overhead.
lisa: also think we should avoid running slow python normalization on the fast path. move normalization to a pre-processing worker or ensure the rust tokenizer path supports our custom normalizers.
sophie: for immediate fix: 1) gate slow normalizer behind a config flag and default to rust path for prod; 2) add a kvcache eviction backpressure metric and an autoscaler tweak to add capacity before eviction spikes.
juan: ops question: what's the rollout risk for disabling slow path? might affect a handful of customers relying on that normalization behavior.
maya: I've got a canary build where we flip `runtime.tokenizer.force_rust=true` for internal-only traffic. perf shows clear improvement. I'll open a PR with the opt-out flag and a migration note.
kevin: also add a perf regression test: simulate 32 streams w/ tunable kvcache size and measure flamegraph diffs; baseline must be kept for next releases.
perf-bot: created perf-issue #4872 referencing this thread and attached fg.svg and nsys snippets.
maya: will follow up with a short postmortem-style note in eng-runtime channel after we validate canary. thanks all :thumbsup:
lisa: nice detective work. can we also annotate the flamegraphs in PerfUI with a note pointing to PR/issue id so future runs have context?
maya: will do, linking #4872 in the flamegraph's metadata and the console trace.
kevin: ping me when PR is ready, i'll review the scheduler spin mitigation changes.
juan: leaving notes to add to the runbook: "if tokenization Py alloc spikes and kvcache evictions >2x baseline -> check tokenizer config + kvcache cap; consider enabling rust tokenizer and increasing kvcache capacity or evict policy." will add to runbook once PR merges.
maya: copying summary: root cause = occasional fallback to python slow normalizer combined with kvcache evictions causing CPU rehydration and scheduler spin -> Py alloc hotspot. Mitigations: prefer rust tokenizer, kvcache capacity smoothing, add perf tests, add metric alarms.
kevin: LGTM."
